title: Matrix-profile-driven attention kernel selector and v2/v3 regression mitigation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Recent rollouts that include FlashAttention v3 kernels have shown intermittent latency regressions and occasional OOMs during large prefill batches. Investigation shows that the v3 workspace allocation behavior is more sensitive to sequence-length skew and contiguous workspace assumptions, while v2 performed better for certain input profile shapes. This ticket proposes a matrix-profile-driven kernel selector: instead of a static heuristic (sequence-length > X -> v3), we compute a small per-request profile (batch histogram of seq_len, per-token decode growth estimate, kv cache hit ratio) to choose the optimal kernel variant and prefill/decode scheduling parameters at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime chooses a kernel variant (v2 or v3 or fallback) based on per-batch matrix profile and logs the decision to tracing
End-to-end p95 generation latency for our internal long-context workload reduces by >= 10% compared to current v3-only baseline or is no worse than v2 baseline (whichever is better)
No increased OOM occurrence in stress tests (1000 runs) compared to v2 baseline
Automated gating test added to CI that reproduces a documented skewed-sequence workload and asserts selector chooses expected kernel
Rollout plan documented with safe rollback and canary criteria
steps_to_reproduce: Use the long-context internal benchmark (link in 'links') with sequence lengths [1024, 2048, 4096] skewed 70/20/10 across a batch of 64
Run prefill-only workload with kv cache warming for 5 minutes, observe peak GPU memory and latency outliers
Compare behavior with kernel_override=flashattn_v2 and kernel_override=flashattn_v3
Run stress harness that sends 200 concurrent requests with variable seq_len distributions to observe OOM/latency failures
experiment_results: Preliminary A/B runs: - Baseline (v3-only): p50=28ms p95=190ms, 3 OOM events in 200 runs. - v2-only: p50=31ms p95=170ms, 0 OOMs. - Matrix-selector prototype (profile-driven): p50=29ms p95=162ms, 0 OOMs. Selector favored v2 for batches with >60% long sequences or high kv-workspace estimates; favored v3 for compact batches where kernel tiling wins. Prototype reduced p95 tail by ~15% vs v3-only and removed OOMs in our stress harness.
perf_summary: Selector reduces tail latency for mixed-length workloads
Eliminates observed OOM spikes in stress tests by preferring conservative kernel or enabling partial-prefill pacing
Adds ~1.8% median latency overhead from profiling computation but yields >10% p95 improvement in worst-case workloads
rollout_plan: 1) Merge selector behind feature flag 'matrix_kernel_selector' and ship to canary pool (5% traffic) for 48h
2) Monitor p50/p95/p99, GPU OOMs, memory headroom, and end-to-end SLOs via runtime-ops dashboard (panel IDs in links)
3) If errors/latency regressions < 2% and no OOMs, expand to 25% for 24h, then 50% for 24h, then 100%
4) Provide emergency rollback flag to force kernel_override to v2 or v3 per-model-instance
5) Post-rollback investigation checklist and kaizen doc link will be attached to the rollout PR
risks: Profiling misestimation could cause selector to pick a suboptimal kernel and increase latency for some classes of requests
Edge-case workspace layout differences between GPU drivers may surface only in specific regions/hardware
Added complexity to runtime selector increases maintenance surface and potential bugs in canary logic
followups: Add an adaptive learning mode: log decisions and outcomes to build an internal model for thresholds (Q2 initiative)
Expose per-model tuning knobs in Redwood Console to override selector thresholds for enterprise customers with strict SLAs
Evaluate adding a micro-batching prefill pacing mechanism to further reduce memory spikes
